6:143: Al-Bukhari said: Musa bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: The bahīrah is the one whose milk is forbidden to the tyrants, so no one among the people milks it, and the sā’ibah they used to leave for their gods, and nothing was carried on it. He said: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Amr ibn Amir Al-Khuza’i dragging his intestines in the fire. He was the first to set free the sa’iba ravenous camels.” The wasilah is the virgin female camel that gives birth early in the first generation of camels, and even gives birth to a female after that. They used to set them free for their idols if one of them was mated with the other and there was no male between them. The haam is the male camel that strikes the counted number of times. When it has finished striking, they leave it for the idols and spare it from pregnancy, so nothing is carried on it, and they call it the haami. Muslim and Al-Nasa’i narrated this in the same way from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa’d. Then Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Yaman told me, Shu’ayb told us from Al-Zuhri, he said: I heard Sa’id narrating this. He said: Abu Hurairah said something similar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Al-Haad narrated it from Ibn Shihab, from Sa’id, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim said: Al-Bukhari wanted Yazid bin Abdullah bin Al-Haad to narrate it on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab bin Bakht, on the authority of Al-Zuhri. This is how our Sheikh Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Mizzi narrated it in Al-A’traf, and he was silent and did not point it out. There is a problem with what Al-Hakim said, because Imam Ahmad and Abu Ja’far bin Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ibn Al-Haad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri himself, and God knows best. Then Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Abi Yaqub Abu Abdullah Al-Karmani told us, Hassan bin Ibrahim told us, Yunus told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Hell crushing each other, and I saw Amr dragging his intestines, and he was the first to set the stray animals free. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Al-Harith told us on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Aktham bin Al-Jun: O Aktham, I saw Amr bin Luhay bin Qama’ah bin Khandaf dragging his intestines in the Fire, and I have never seen a man more similar to another man than you to him, nor to him than you. Aktham said: Are you afraid that his resemblance will harm me, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No, you are a believer and he is an unbeliever. He was the first to change the religion of Abraham, and the sea of the lake, and the freed slave, and the protected protector.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Hanad, on the authority of Abdah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar or similar manner. These two paths are not in the books. Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Mujammi’ narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hijri narrated to us, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The first to set free the sa’iba and worship idols was Abu Khuza’ah Amr ibn Amir, and I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I know the first to set free the sa’iba and the first to change the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him.” They said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said: “Amr ibn Luhay, the brother of Banu Ka’b. I saw him dragging his intestines in the Fire, his smell bothering the people of the Fire, and I know the first to open the seas.” They said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said, “A man from Banu Mudlij had two she-camels. He cut off their ears and forbade them from milking them. Then he drank their milk after that. I saw him in the fire while they were biting him with their mouths and trampling him with their hooves.” This Amr is the son of Luhay ibn Qama’ah, one of the leaders of Khuza’ah who took charge of the House after Jurhum. He was the first to change the religion of Abraham, the friend of God. He introduced idols to the Hijaz and called upon the common people to worship them and seek closeness through them. He established for them these pre-Islamic laws regarding livestock and other things, as God Almighty mentioned in Surat Al-An’am when He said, And they assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock. to the end of the verses on that. As for the bahīrah, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: It is a female camel that has given birth to five offspring. They look at the fifth, and if it is a male, they slaughter it. The men eat it, but not the women. If it is a female, they cut off its ears and say: This is a bahīrah. As-Suddi and others mentioned something similar to this. As for the sa’ibah, Mujahid said that it is a type of sheep similar to what was explained about the bahīrah, except that it did not give birth to a child and there were six children between them. It remained in its form. If it gave birth to the seventh, a male or two, they slaughtered it. The men ate it, but not the women. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The sa’ibah is a female camel that has given birth to ten female offspring, none of whom were male. It was left unattended and not ridden, its hair was not cut, and its milk was not milked except for a guest. Abu Ruq said: The sa’ibah was that if a man went out and satisfied his need, he would leave a female camel or something else from his wealth and give it to the tyrants. Whatever it gave birth to was its own. Al-Suddi said: If a man among them had his need met, or recovered from an illness, or his wealth increased, he would leave some of his wealth for the idols. If any of the people encountered him, he would be punished with a punishment in this world. As for the wasila, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is a sheep that has given birth to seven wombs. They look at the seventh. If it is a male or female and it is dead, the men share in it but not the women. If it is a female, they spare it. If it is a male and a female in one womb, they spare them both and say: His sister joined him, so he is forbidden to us. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: And no wasila. He said: The wasila from the camels is the female camel that gave birth first to a female, then gave birth to a female, so they called her the wasila. They say: She joined two females with no male between them, so they would cut off her throat for their idols. This is also narrated on the authority of Imam Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The wasila from the sheep if it gives birth to ten females in five wombs, twins in each womb, is called the wasila and is left. Any male or female that is born after that is given to the males but not the females. If it is dead, they share in it. As for the Hami: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If a man had inseminated his stallion ten times, it would be said: He has become Hami, so leave him. Abu Rawq and Qatadah said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: As for the Hami, it is the male camel that when he gives birth to his offspring, they say: This one has become Hami on his back, so they do not burden him with anything, nor do they cut off his hair, nor do they prevent him from a pasture or a watering place from which he can drink, even if the watering place does not belong to his owner. Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik say: As for the Hami, it is the camel. It used to strike camels, and when his strike was over, they would put peacock feathers on it and let it go. Other than that has been said in the interpretation of this verse. There is a hadith in this regard narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas al-Jashmi, on the authority of his father Malik ibn Nadlah, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing two pieces of clothing, and he said to me: Do you have any wealth? I said: Yes. He said: From what wealth? I said: “From all wealth: camels, sheep, horses, and slaves.” He said: So if God gives you wealth and it increases for you, then he said: Do your camels give birth with their ears intact? I said: Yes, do camels give birth except in this way? He said: “Perhaps you will take a razor and cut off the ears of a group of them and say: ‘This is a bahīrah,’ and slit the ears of a group of them and say: ‘This is a sanctuary.’” I said: Yes. He said: Then do not do that, for everything that God has given you is permissible for you. Then he said: God has not made bahīrah, sa’ībah, wasīlah, or Ḥām. As for the lake, it is the one whose ears they cut off, so that his wife, daughters, and none of his family will benefit from its wool, fur, hair, or milk. When it dies, they share in it. As for the one who is free, she is the one who is left for their gods and goes to their gods and leaves them. As for the one who is left, the ewe gives birth to six wombs, and when she gives birth to the seventh, her horn is cut off, and they say: She has arrived, so they do not slaughter her, nor is she beaten or prevented whenever she comes to a pond. This is how the explanation of that is mentioned, inserted in the hadith. Another version was narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas Aouf bin Malik, from his statement, and it is more similar. This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Abu Al-Zura’a Amr bin Amr, on the authority of his uncle Abu Al-Ahwas Aouf bin Malik bin Nadlah, on the authority of his father, and it does not contain an explanation of this, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: But those who disbelieve invent lies about God, and most of them do not reason. That is, God did not legislate these things, nor do they bring Him closer to Him. Rather, the polytheists fabricated them and made them a law for themselves and a means of drawing closer to Him. But that is not what they will achieve, rather it is a disaster for them. And when it is said to them, ‘Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger,’ they say, ‘Sufficient for us is that which we found our fathers following.’ That is, when they are called to the religion of God and His law and what He has made obligatory, and to abandon what He has forbidden, they say, Sufficient for us is that which we found our fathers and grandfathers following of ways and paths. God the Almighty says: Or even if their fathers did not know anything? That is, they did not understand the truth, nor did they know it, nor were they guided to it. So how can they follow them in this case? None follows them except those who are more ignorant than them and further astray. This is a statement of the ignorance of the Arabs before Islam, regarding what they forbade from livestock and made them parts and types such as Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, Ham, and other types that they invented in livestock, crops and fruits. So God the Almighty explained that He created gardens with trellises and without trellises, and that He created from livestock a burden and a bed, then He explained the types of livestock into sheep, which is white, which is the lamb, and black, which is the male and female goat, and camels, male and female, and cows as well, and that God the Almighty did not forbid any of that or any of their children, rather all of them were created for the children of Adam to eat, ride, carry, milk and other types of benefits, as He said, "And He has sent down for you from the livestock eight mates" verse. And His statement, the Almighty: "As for what the wombs of the two females contain verse is a response to their saying, What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives" verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful. That is, tell me with certainty how God forbade you what you claimed to have forbidden, such as the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, the ḥām, and the like. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, Eight pairs of sheep, two, and of goats, two, so these are four pairs. Say, ‘Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?’ He says, Is it not that the wombs of the two females contain? Meaning, does the womb contain anything but a male or a female? Why do you forbid some and permit others? Inform Me with knowledge, if you should be truthful? God Almighty says, It is all lawful. And God Almighty says, Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you? He mocks them for what they innovated and fabricated against God of forbidding what they forbade of that. Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? That is, no one is more unjust than them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. The first to be included in this verse was Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama’ah, because he was the first to change the religion of the prophets and the first to set free the stray animals, connect the connected ones, and protect the protected ones, as is proven in the Sahih.
6:139: Abu Ishaq al-Subai'i said on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Hudhayl on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they said, 'What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males,' the verse means milk. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they said, 'What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males,' meaning milk. They used to forbid their females from it, but their males used to drink it. When a sheep gave birth to a male, they would slaughter it, and it was for the men but not the women. If it was a female, it would be left and not slaughtered. If it was dead, they would share in it. So God forbade that. Al-Suddi said the same. Al-Sha’bi said: Only men can eat the milk of the lake, and if any of it dies, both men and women can eat it. This is what Ikrimah, Qatadah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. Mujahid said about His statement, And they say, ‘What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives,’ he said, They are the Sa’iba and the Bahira. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid and Qatadah said about God’s statement, He will recompense them for their description, meaning their false statement in that, meaning like His statement, the Most High, “And do not say about what your tongues describe falsely, ‘This is lawful and this is unlawful,’ to invent a lie about God. Indeed, those who invent a lie about God will not succeed. Enjoyment,” the verse, He is Wise, meaning in His actions, words, law and decree, Knowing of the deeds of His servants, good and evil, and He will recompense them for them with the most complete recompense.
6:140: God the Almighty says: Those who committed these actions have lost in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, they lost their children by killing them, and their wealth was restricted, so they forbade things they invented of their own accord. As for the Hereafter, they will end up in the worst of positions because of their lies and fabrications against God, as God the Almighty says: “Indeed, those who invent lies against God will not succeed. Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said in his interpretation of this verse: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim told us, Muhammad bin Ayoub told us, Abd al-Rahman bin al-Mubarak told us, Abu Awana told us on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: If you want to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then read what is above one hundred and thirty from Surat al-An’am 6:Indeed, those who kill their children foolishly without knowledge and forbid what God has provided for them, inventing a lie against God have gone astray and they were not… “Guided.” And thus Al-Bukhari narrated it alone in the Book of the Virtues of Quraysh in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu Al-Nu’man Muhammad ibn Al-Fadl A’rim, on the authority of Abu Awana, whose name is Al-Waddah ibn Abdullah Al-Yashkari, on the authority of Abu Bishr, whose name is Ja’far ibn Abi Wahshiyya, ibn Iyas, on his authority.
6:141: The Almighty says, explaining that He is the Creator of everything from crops, fruits, and livestock that these polytheists have disposed of with their corrupt opinions, and divided and divided them, making some of them permissible and some of them forbidden. He said, And it is He who has produced gardens, trellised and untrellised. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Trellised and untrellised. In another narration, the trellised are what people have trellised, and the untrellised are what grows in the land and mountains of fruits. Ata’ al-Khurasani said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Trellised are what is trellised from the grapevine, and the untrellised are what is not trellised from the grapevine. Al-Suddi said the same. Ibn Jurayj said, Similar and dissimilar, he said, Similar in appearance and dissimilar in taste. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said, Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, he said, From its dates and grapes. And the Almighty’s saying, And give its due on the day of its harvest, Ibn Jarir said, Some of them said it is the obligatory zakat. Amr told us, he told us, Abdul Samad, Yazid bin Dirham told us, he said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: And give its due on the day of its harvest. He said: The obligatory zakat. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And give its due on the day of its harvest, meaning the obligatory zakat on the day it is measured and its measure is known. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And give its due on the day of its harvest, that is, when a man planted, and on the day of his harvest he did not produce anything from what he harvested, so God Almighty said, And give its due on the day of its harvest, that is, he knows what his measure and his due from every ten is one, and what people pick from its spike. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban told me, on the authority of his uncle Was’ bin Habban, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered from every harvester ten wasqs of dates to be hung in the mosque for the poor. This is a good, strong chain of transmission. Tawus, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: It is zakat. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It is charity from grain and fruits. Zaid bin Aslam said the same, and others said: It is another right besides zakat. Ash’ath said: On the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin and Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: They used to give something other than zakat. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and others narrated on the authority of Abdul-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah regarding his statement, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: He gives whoever is present on that day what is easy, and it is not zakat. Mujahid said: If the poor are present to you, you give them some of it. Abdul-Razzaq said on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: When planting, he gives a handful, and when harvesting, he gives a handful, and he leaves them to follow the traces of harvesting. Al-Thawri said: On the authority of Hammad on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, he said: He gives like a bunch. Ibn al-Mubarak said on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Salim on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: This was before zakat. The poor were given a handful and a bunch for fodder for their beasts. In the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah: On the authority of Daraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Saeed, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, And give its due on the day of its harvest. He said, What falls from the ears of corn. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Others said: This was something that was obligatory, then God abrogated it by a tenth or half a tenth. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, Atiyah Al-Awfi, and others. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose it. I said: There is some doubt about calling this abrogation, because it was something that was obligatory in the original, then He explained it in detail and clarified the amount of the output and its quantity. They said: This was in the second year of the Hijrah, and God knows best. God the Almighty has condemned those who harvest and do not give in charity, as He mentioned about the people of Paradise in Surah Nun: “When they swore to harvest it in the morning, and they made no exception. Then a company from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep. And it became like a black, scorched night. And they called to one another in the morning, ‘Go forth to your tillage, if you are harvesters.’ So they set out, whispering, ‘Let no poor person enter it today upon you.’ And they went forth in the morning, strong, resolute, and determined. But when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ Rather, we are deprived. The most middle of them said, ‘Did I not tell you, “Why do you not glorify God?”’ They said, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ So they turned to one another, blaming each other. They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors! Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us one better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord aspiring.’ Such is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.” And the Almighty’s saying: And do not be extravagant, for He does not like the extravagant. It was said that its meaning is do not be extravagant in giving, so that you give more than is appropriate. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They used to give something on the day of harvest, then they competed over it and were extravagant, so God revealed: And do not be extravagant. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, who cut down his palm trees and said: No one will come to me today except that I will feed him, so he fed him until evening and he had no fruit, so God revealed: And do not be extravagant, for He does not like the extravagant. Narrated by Ibn Jarir from him. Ibn Jurayj said from Ata’: They forbade extravagance in everything. Iyas bin Mu’awiyah said: Whatever you exceed the command of God is extravagance. Al-Suddi said regarding His saying: And do not be extravagant, he said: Do not give your money and remain poor. Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab and Muhammad bin Ka’b said regarding His saying: And do not be extravagant, he said: Do not withhold charity and disobey your Lord. Then Ibn Jarir chose the saying of Ata’, that He forbade extravagance in everything, without a doubt. It is true, but it appears, and God knows best, from the context of the verse, where God Almighty said: Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit and give its due on the day of its harvest, and be not excessive, that it refers to eating, meaning do not be excessive in eating because of the harm it causes to the mind and body, as God Almighty said: Eat and drink, but be not excessive, the verse. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, there is a comment: Eat, drink and dress without extravagance or vanity. This is from this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And of the livestock are loads and furnishings. That is, He created for you from the livestock what is loads and what is furnishings. It was said that what is meant by the load is what is carried on from the camels, and the furnishings are the young ones among them, as Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah in his saying: The load is what is carried on from the camels and the furnishings are the young ones among the camels. Al-Hakim narrated it and said its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it. Ibn Abbas said: The load is the large ones and the furnishings are the young ones among the camels, and Mujahid said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And of the livestock are loads and furnishings. As for the load, it is camels, horses, mules, donkeys and everything that is carried on, and as for the furnishings, it is sheep, and Ibn Jarir chose it. He said: I think it was called furnishings because of its proximity to the ground. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: The load is the camels and cows and the furnishings are the sheep. And he said: As-Suddi: As for the load, it is camels, and as for the fursh, it is the two young camels, the ajajil, and the sheep. Whatever is carried on it is a load. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The load is what you ride, and the fursh is what you eat and milk. A sheep that does not carry, you eat its meat and make a blanket and a furnishing from its wool. What Abd al-Rahman said in the interpretation of this noble verse is good, as is supported by the Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, so they own them? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat. And the Almighty said: “And indeed, in the livestock is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excrement and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers.” Until he said: And from their wool and their fur and their hair - furnishings and provisions for a time. God the Almighty said: “It is God who has made for you the grazing livestock that you may ride on them and eat from them. And there are benefits for you in them and that you may attain through them a need in your hearts and on them and on ships you are carried. And He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of God do you deny?” And God the Almighty said: Eat of what God has provided for you meaning fruits, crops and livestock, for God created them all and made them a provision for you. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan meaning his path and commands as the polytheists followed them who forbade what God provided for them, meaning fruits and crops, fabricating against God. Indeed, Satan is to you a clear enemy meaning his apparent enmity is clear, as God the Almighty said: “Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze” and God the Almighty said: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts and God the Almighty said: Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are to you an enemy? Evil are the wrongdoers. Instead, there are many verses in the Qur’an about this.
6:142: The Almighty says, explaining that He is the Creator of everything from crops, fruits, and livestock that these polytheists have disposed of with their corrupt opinions, and divided and divided them, making some of them permissible and some of them forbidden. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And give its due on the day of its harvest, meaning the obligatory zakat on the day it is measured and its measure is known. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And give its due on the day of its harvest, that is, when a man planted, and on the day of his harvest he did not produce anything from what he harvested, so God Almighty said, And give its due on the day of its harvest, that is, he knows what his measure and his due from every ten is one, and what people pick from its spike. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban told me, on the authority of his uncle Was’ bin Habban, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered from every harvester ten wasqs of dates to be hung in the mosque for the poor. This is a good, strong chain of transmission. Tawus, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: It is zakat. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It is charity from grain and fruits. Zaid bin Aslam said the same, and others said: It is another right besides zakat. Ash’ath said: On the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin and Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar regarding his statement, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: They used to give something other than zakat. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and others narrated on the authority of Abdul-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah regarding his statement, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: He gives whoever is present on that day what is easy, and it is not zakat. Mujahid said: If the poor are present to you, you give them some of it. Abdul-Razzaq said on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: When planting, he gives a handful, and when harvesting, he gives a handful, and he leaves them to follow the traces of harvesting. Al-Thawri said: On the authority of Hammad on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, he said: He gives like a bunch. Ibn al-Mubarak said on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Salim on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, And give its due on the day of its harvest, he said: This was before zakat. The poor were given a handful and a bunch for fodder for their beasts. In the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah: On the authority of Daraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Saeed, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, And give its due on the day of its harvest. He said, What falls from the ears of corn. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Others said: This was something that was obligatory, then God abrogated it by a tenth or half a tenth. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, Atiyah Al-Awfi, and others. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, chose it. I said: There is some doubt about calling this abrogation, because it was something that was obligatory in the original, then He explained it in detail and clarified the amount of the output and its quantity. They said: This was in the second year of the Hijrah, and God knows best. God the Almighty has condemned those who harvest and do not give in charity, as He mentioned about the people of Paradise in Surah Nun: “When they swore to harvest it in the morning, and they made no exception. Then a company from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep. And it became like a black, scorched night. And they called to one another in the morning, ‘Go forth to your tillage, if you are harvesters.’ So they set out, whispering, ‘Let no poor person enter it today upon you.’ And they went forth in the morning, strong, resolute, and determined. But when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ Rather, we are deprived. The most middle of them said, ‘Did I not tell you, “Why do you not glorify God?”’ They said, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ So they turned to one another, blaming each other. They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors! Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us one better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord aspiring.’ Such is the punishment, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.” And the Almighty’s saying: And do not be extravagant, for He does not like the extravagant. It was said that its meaning is do not be extravagant in giving, so that you give more than is appropriate. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They used to give something on the day of harvest, then they competed over it and were extravagant, so God revealed: And do not be extravagant. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, who cut down his palm trees and said: No one will come to me today except that I will feed him, so he fed him until evening and he had no fruit, so God revealed: And do not be extravagant, for He does not like the extravagant. Narrated by Ibn Jarir from him. Ibn Jurayj said from Ata’: They forbade extravagance in everything. Iyas bin Mu’awiyah said: Whatever you exceed the command of God is extravagance. Al-Suddi said regarding His saying: And do not be extravagant, he said: Do not give your money and remain poor. Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab and Muhammad bin Ka’b said regarding His saying: And do not be extravagant, he said: Do not withhold charity and disobey your Lord. Then Ibn Jarir chose the saying of Ata’, that He forbade extravagance in everything, without a doubt. It is true, but it appears, and God knows best, from the context of the verse, where God Almighty said: Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit and give its due on the day of its harvest, and be not excessive, that it refers to eating, meaning do not be excessive in eating because of the harm it causes to the mind and body, as God Almighty said: Eat and drink, but be not excessive, the verse. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, there is a comment: Eat, drink and dress without extravagance or vanity. This is from this, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And of the livestock are loads and furnishings. That is, He created for you from the livestock what is loads and what is furnishings. It was said that what is meant by the load is what is carried on from the camels, and the furnishings are the young ones among them, as Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah in his saying: The load is what is carried on from the camels and the furnishings are the young ones among the camels. Al-Hakim narrated it and said its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it. Ibn Abbas said: The load is the large ones and the furnishings are the young ones among the camels, and Mujahid said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And of the livestock are loads and furnishings. As for the load, it is camels, horses, mules, donkeys and everything that is carried on, and as for the furnishings, it is sheep, and Ibn Jarir chose it. He said: I think it was called furnishings because of its proximity to the ground. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: The load is the camels and cows and the furnishings are the sheep. And he said: As-Suddi: As for the load, it is camels, and as for the fursh, it is the two young camels, the ajajil, and the sheep. Whatever is carried on it is a load. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The load is what you ride, and the fursh is what you eat and milk. A sheep that does not carry, you eat its meat and make a blanket and a furnishing from its wool. What Abd al-Rahman said in the interpretation of this noble verse is good, as is supported by the Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, so they own them? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat. And the Almighty said: “And indeed, in the livestock is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excrement and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers.” Until he said: And from their wool and their fur and their hair - furnishings and provisions for a time. God the Almighty said: “It is God who has made for you the grazing livestock that you may ride on them and eat from them. And there are benefits for you in them and that you may attain through them a need in your hearts and on them and on ships you are carried. And He shows you His signs. So which of the signs of God do you deny?” And God the Almighty said: Eat of what God has provided for you meaning fruits, crops and livestock, for God created them all and made them a provision for you. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan meaning his path and commands as the polytheists followed them who forbade what God provided for them, meaning fruits and crops, fabricating against God. Indeed, Satan is to you a clear enemy meaning his apparent enmity is clear, as God the Almighty said: “Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze” and God the Almighty said: O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts and God the Almighty said: Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are to you an enemy? Evil are the wrongdoers. Instead, there are many verses in the Qur’an about this.
6:144: This is a statement of the ignorance of the Arabs before Islam, regarding what they forbade from livestock and made them parts and types such as Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, Ham, and other types that they invented in livestock, crops and fruits. So God the Almighty explained that He created gardens with trellises and without trellises, and that He created from livestock a burden and a bed, then He explained the types of livestock into sheep, which is white, which is the lamb, and black, which is the male and female goat, and camels, male and female, and cows as well, and that God the Almighty did not forbid any of that or any of their children, rather all of them were created for the children of Adam to eat, ride, carry, milk and other types of benefits, as He said, And He has sent down for you from the livestock eight mates verse. And His statement, the Almighty: As for what the wombs of the two females contain verse is a response to their saying, What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives verse. And the Almighty’s saying: Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful. That is, tell me with certainty how God forbade you what you claimed to have forbidden, such as the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, the ḥām, and the like. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, Eight pairs of sheep, two, and of goats, two, so these are four pairs. Say, ‘Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?’ He says, Is it not that the wombs of the two females contain? Meaning, does the womb contain anything but a male or a female? Why do you forbid some and permit others? Inform Me with knowledge, if you should be truthful? God Almighty says, It is all lawful. And God Almighty says, Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you? He mocks them for what they innovated and fabricated against God of forbidding what they forbade of that. Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? That is, no one is more unjust than them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. The first to be included in this verse was Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama’ah, because he was the first to change the religion of the prophets and the first to set free the stray animals, connect the connected ones, and protect the protected ones, as is proven in the Sahih.
6:145: God Almighty says, commanding His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to those who have forbidden what God has provided for them, inventing falsehoods against God, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it, meaning one who eats it. It has been said that its meaning is, I do not find anything of what you have forbidden forbidden except this, and it has been said that its meaning is, I do not find any of the animals forbidden except this. Based on this, what was mentioned of the prohibitions after this in Surat Al-Ma’idah and in the hadiths that were mentioned removes the meaning of this verse. Some people call this abrogation, but most of the later scholars do not call it abrogation because it is a matter of removing something originally permissible, and God knows best. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, or spilled blood, meaning shed blood. Akrima said about his statement, or spilled blood, if it were not for this verse, people would have followed what is in the veins as the Jews did. Hammad said on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr who said: I asked Abu Majlaz about blood, and what is stained from the head of the slaughtered animal, and about the cooking pot in which the redness is seen? He said: God only forbade spilled blood. Qatada said: What is forbidden of blood is what is spilled, but as for meat mixed with blood, there is no problem with it. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told us, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she did not see anything wrong with the meat of wild animals, but the redness and blood that are on the cooking pot are wrong, and she recited this verse. Sahih Gharib. Al-Hamidi said: Sufyan told us, Amr ibn Dinar told us, he said: I said to Jabir ibn Abdullah: They claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the meat of domesticated donkeys at the time of Khaybar, so he said: Al-Hakam ibn Amr used to say that on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but the rabbi, meaning Ibn Abbas, refused that and recited: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it” the verse, and this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Madini on the authority of Sufyan on his authority, and Abu Dawud included it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak even though it is in Sahih Al-Bukhari as you have seen. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Duhaim told us, Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, Muhammad bin Sharik told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Al-Shathaa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to eat some things and leave others out of disgust, so God sent His Prophet and revealed His Book and made lawful what He made lawful and forbade what He made unlawful. So whatever He made lawful is lawful, whatever He forbade is unlawful, and whatever He was silent about is pardoned. And he recited this verse: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]. This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Dawud narrated it alone, on the authority of Muhammad bin Dawud bin Subaih, on the authority of Abu Naim, and Al-Hakim said: This is a hadith with a sound chain of transmission, and they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A sheep belonging to Sawda bint Zam’ah died, so she said: O Messenger of God, so-and-so died, meaning The sheep. He said, Why didn’t you take its musk? She said, Shall we take the musk of a sheep that had died? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, God only said, ‘Say, “I do not find in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it, unless it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine. And you would not eat it unless you tan it and benefit from it.’” So she sent and skinned its musk, tanned it, and made a water skin from it until it was torn apart by her. Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari, and al-Nasa’i, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Sawdah bint Zam’ah, with that or something similar. Saeed bin Mansour said: Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us on the authority of Isa bin Numailah Al-Fazari on the authority of his father, who said: I was with Ibn Omar when a man asked him about eating hedgehogs, so he recited to him: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it” 10:13. Then an old man with him said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: It was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: An evil among the evils. Ibn Omar said: If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it, then it is as he said. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu Thawr on the authority of Saeed bin Mansour on his authority. And the Almighty said: But whoever is forced by necessity, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] meaning, whoever is forced to eat something that God has forbidden in this noble verse, and he is not engaged in transgression or aggression, then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful meaning, He is Forgiving and Merciful to him. The interpretation of this verse has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah sufficiently. The purpose of the context of this noble verse is to respond to the polytheists who innovated what they innovated of forbidding forbidden things for themselves, with their corrupt opinions of the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, the ḥām, and the like. So He ordered His Messenger to inform them that he did not find in what God revealed to him that this was forbidden. Rather, He forbade what was mentioned in this verse of dead animals, spilled blood, the flesh of swine, and that which was dedicated to other than God. And other than that, He did not forbid it, but rather it is pardoned and kept silent about. So how do you claim that it is forbidden? And from where did you forbid it while God did not forbid it? Therefore, there is no prohibition of other things after this, just as the prohibition of the meat of domesticated donkeys, the meat of wild animals, and every bird with talons came according to the well-known schools of thought of scholars.
6:146: Ibn Jarir said, God Almighty says: And We forbade the Jews every animal with claws, which is the beasts and birds, unless they have split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese and ducks. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, which is the camel and the ostrich. Mujahid and al-Suddi said the same in one narration. Saeed bin Jubayr said: It is that which does not have split toes. In another narration from him, everything with split toes, including the rooster. Qatada said in his statement, And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and the camel and ostrich and some birds and whales were called, and in another narration, the camel and the ostrich. And He forbade them from birds, ducks and the like, and everything that does not have split toes. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: Everything with claws. He said: The ostrich and the camel are shaqashqan. I said to al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, and I told him, what is shaqashqan? He said: Everything that does not spread out from the legs of animals. He said: What do you eat that does spread out? He said: The legs of animals and birds spread out. He said: So the Jews eat it. He said: The leg of the camel - its hoof - does not spread out, nor the hoof of the ostrich, nor the leg of the goose. So the Jews do not eat camels, nor ostriches, nor geese, nor anything whose leg does not spread out, nor do they eat the wild donkey. And the Almighty’s statement: And of the cows and the sheep We have forbidden them their fat, As-Suddi said: He means the omentum and the fat of the kidneys. The Jews used to say that Israel forbade it, so we forbid it. Ibn Zayd said the same. Qatada said: The omentum and all fat that is like that is not on a bone. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except what their backs carry meaning what is attached to the back of the fat. Al-Suddi and Abu Saleh said: The buttocks are what their backs carry. The Almighty said: Or the entrails Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Al-Hawaya is the plural of Hawiya, Hawiya, and Hawiya, and it is what the stomach contains and it gathers and becomes round. They are the daughters of milk, which are the camels’ quarters and are called Al-Marabd, and the intestines are in them. He said: The meaning of the statement is: And from the cows and sheep, We have forbidden them their fat except what their backs carry or what the entrails carry. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or the entrails, which are the camels’ quarters. Mujahid said: Al-Hawaya is the camels’ quarters and the resting place. This is what Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abu Malik, Al-Suddi said. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others said: Al-Hawaya are the resting places in which the intestines are located, in the middle of them, and they are the daughters of milk. In the speech of the Arabs, it is called Al-Marabd. The Almighty said: Or what is mixed with a bone meaning except what is mixed with fat with a bone, for we have permitted it for them. He said: Ibn Jurayj: The fat of the buttocks, which is mixed with the coccyx, is permissible. Everything in the legs, sides, head, and eyes, and whatever is mixed with a bone, is permissible, and so on. This was stated by Al-Suddi. And the statement of God the Almighty: That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, meaning that this constriction was done to them and We imposed it on them as recompense for their transgression and disobedience to Our commands, as God the Almighty said: Then because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We prohibited to them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them, and because of their averting [people] from the way of God much. And His statement: And indeed, We are truthful, meaning, We are just in what We recompense them with. Ibn Jarir said: And indeed, We are truthful in what We have told you, O Muhammad, about Our prohibition of that upon them, not as they claimed, that it was Israel who prohibited it upon himself. And God knows best. Abdullah bin Abbas said: It reached Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that Samurah sold wine, so he said: May God curse Samurah, did he not know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God cursed the Jews, and they forbade them from fat, so they rendered it and sold it? They narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, from Amr bin Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar, with it. Al-Layth said: Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, he said: Ata bin Abi Rabah said: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say in the year of the conquest: God and His Messenger forbade the sale of wine, dead animals, pigs, and idols. It was said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the fat of dead animals, for it is used to grease hides, coat ships, and people use it for lighting? He said: No, it is forbidden. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at that time: May God curse the Jews, for when God forbade them from their fat, they rendered it, sold it, and ate its price. The group narrated it from various chains of narration on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib with it. Al-Zuhri said: On the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: May God curse the Jews! Fat was forbidden to them, so they sold it and ate its price. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it, on the authority of Abdun, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on his authority. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ibrahim told us, Ismail ibn Ishaq told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Wahb told us, Khalid al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Barakah Abu al-Walid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting behind the Maqam, and he raised his eyes to the sky and said: May God curse the Jews three times. God forbade them fat, so they sold it and ate its price. God has not forbidden a people to eat something without forbidding them its price. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Asim told us, Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Barakah Abu Al-Walid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the mosque facing the Black Stone, and he looked at the sky and laughed and said: “May God curse the Jews, for they forbade them the fat, so they sold it and ate its price. When God forbids a people from eating something, He forbids them its price.” Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Khalid Al-Hadha’. Al-A’mash said: On the authority of Jami’ bin Shaddad, on the authority of Kulthum, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, who said: We entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sick, to visit him. We found him sleeping, his face covered with an Adani cloak, so he uncovered his face and said: May God curse the Jews, for they forbade the fat of sheep and ate its price. In another narration: The fat was forbidden to them, so they sold it and ate its price. In a wording of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When God forbids eating something, He forbids them its price.
6:147: God the Almighty says: If your opponents, O Muhammad, from among the polytheists, Jews and those like them, deny you, “Say: Your Lord is full of vast mercy.” This is an encouragement for them to seek God’s vast mercy and follow His Messenger, His punishment is not averted from the criminal people. This is a warning to them against opposing the Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets. God the Almighty often combines encouragement and warning in the Qur’an, as He the Almighty said at the end of this Surah: Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful. He also said: “And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. Indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.” He also said: “Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment.” He also said: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, severe in penalty. He also said: “Indeed, the wrath of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who initiates and restores. And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.” There are many verses on this subject.
6:148: This is a debate that God Almighty mentioned, and a doubt that the polytheists clung to in their polytheism and prohibition of what they prohibited, for God is aware of what they are in of polytheism and prohibition of what they prohibited, and He is able to change it by inspiring us with faith and standing between us and disbelief, but He did not change it, so it indicates that it is by His will and desire and His approval of us with that, and for this reason they said, If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything, as in the Almighty’s saying, And they said, ‘If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them,’ the verse, and likewise the verse in An-Nahl is similar to this. God the Almighty said: Thus did those before them deny meaning, by this doubt, those who went astray before them went astray. It is a false and invalid argument, because if it were correct, God would not have made them taste His punishment, destroyed them, defeated His noble messengers, and made the polytheists taste painful vengeance. “Say: Do you have any knowledge?” meaning that God is pleased with you in what you are doing. You should bring it forth to us meaning that you should show it to us, clarify it, and present it. You follow nothing but conjecture meaning illusion and imagination. What is meant by conjecture here is corrupt belief. And you are only guessing you lie about God in what you claim. Ali bin Abi Talhah said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: If God had willed, we would not have associated and he said: Thus did those before them deny then he said: And if God had willed, they would not have associated for they said: Our worship of deities brings us closer to God, so God informed them that it does not bring them closer. So His statement: And if God had willed, they would not have associated means God the Almighty says: If I had willed, I would have gathered them all together on guidance. And the Almighty says: “Say: To God belongs the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.” The Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say to them, O Muhammad, To God belongs the conclusive argument. That is, He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive argument in guiding whomever He has guided and misguiding whomever has gone astray. If He had willed, He could have guided you all. All of that is by His power, will, and choice, and He is pleased with the believers and hates the disbelievers, as the Almighty says: And if God had willed, He could have gathered them together upon guidance. And the Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed. And His saying: “And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ. Except whom your Lord has given mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: “I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.” Ad-Dahhak said: No argument has been made for anyone who disobeys God, but God has the conclusive argument for His servants. And the Almighty says: “Say: Bring your witnesses.” That is, bring your witnesses. Who testify that God has forbidden this. That is, this is what you have forbidden, lied about, and fabricated against God about. But if they testify, do not testify with them, meaning that they are only testifying in this case falsely and deceitfully. And do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter and set up equals with their Lord, meaning that they associate others with Him and make equals for Him.
6:149: This is a debate that God Almighty mentioned, and a doubt that the polytheists clung to in their polytheism and prohibition of what they prohibited, for God is aware of what they are in of polytheism and prohibition of what they prohibited, and He is able to change it by inspiring us with faith and standing between us and disbelief, but He did not change it, so it indicates that it is by His will and desire and His approval of us with that, and for this reason they said, If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything], nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything, as in the Almighty’s saying, And they said, ‘If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them,’ the verse, and likewise the verse in An-Nahl is similar to this. God the Almighty said: Thus did those before them deny meaning, by this doubt, those who went astray before them went astray. It is a false and invalid argument, because if it were correct, God would not have made them taste His punishment, destroyed them, defeated His noble messengers, and made the polytheists taste painful vengeance. “Say: Do you have any knowledge?” meaning that God is pleased with you in what you are doing. You should bring it forth to us meaning that you should show it to us, clarify it, and present it. You follow nothing but conjecture meaning illusion and imagination. What is meant by conjecture here is corrupt belief. And you are only guessing you lie about God in what you claim. Ali bin Abi Talhah said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: If God had willed, we would not have associated and he said: Thus did those before them deny then he said: And if God had willed, they would not have associated for they said: Our worship of deities brings us closer to God, so God informed them that it does not bring them closer. So His statement: And if God had willed, they would not have associated means God the Almighty says: If I had willed, I would have gathered them all together on guidance. And the Almighty says: “Say: To God belongs the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.” The Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say to them, O Muhammad, To God belongs the conclusive argument. That is, He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive argument in guiding whomever He has guided and misguiding whomever has gone astray. If He had willed, He could have guided you all. All of that is by His power, will, and choice, and He is pleased with the believers and hates the disbelievers, as the Almighty says: And if God had willed, He could have gathered them together upon guidance. And the Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed. And His saying: “And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ. Except whom your Lord has given mercy. And for that He created them.
