6:151: Dawud al-Awdi said on the authority of al-Sha'bi on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whoever wants to look at the will of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on which his seal is, let him read these verses: "Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We will provide for you and for them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. This He has enjoined upon you that you may understand.'" Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Bakr bin Muhammad al-Sayrafi told us in Marw, Abd al-Samad bin al-Fadl told us, Malik bin Ismail al-Nahdi told us, Israel told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: In al-An'am there are clear verses that are the mother of the Book, then he recited: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.' The verses, then al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. I said: It was narrated by Zuhair and Qais bin Al-Rabi’, both of them on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abdullah bin Qais on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Al-Hakim also narrated in his Musnad, from the hadith of Yazid bin Harun, from Sufyan bin Husayn, from Al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Which of you will pledge allegiance to me on three things?” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you,” until he finished the verses: “So whoever fulfills them, his reward is with God. And whoever falls short of them and God catches him up with it in this world, his punishment will be. And whoever is delayed until the Hereafter, his affair is with God. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him.” Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Rather, they agreed on the hadith of Al-Zuhri, from Abu Idris, from Ubadah, Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God. The hadith. Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated both hadiths, so it should not be attributed to delusion in one of the hadiths if they are combined, and God knows best. As for its interpretation, God the Almighty says: To His Prophet and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worshipped other than God and forbade what God provided for them and killed their children, and they did all of that based on their opinions and the insinuations of the devils to them, Say to them, Come, meaning come and approach, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you, meaning I will tell you and inform you of what your Lord has forbidden you truly, not as a guess or conjecture, but as a revelation from Him and a command from Him, that you do not associate anything with Him, as if there is something omitted in the speech indicated by the context, and its meaning is, And He enjoined upon you, “that you do not associate anything with Him,” and for this reason He said at the end of the verse, This is what He enjoined upon you that you may understand. And as the poet said: He went on pilgrimage and ordered Salma Al-Abed not to see or talk to anyone. And her drink remains cold The Arabs say: I ordered you not to get up. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gabriel came to me and gave me the good report that whoever of your nation dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise. I said: Even if he commits adultery and steals? He said: Even if he commits adultery and steals. I said: Even if he commits adultery and steals? He said: Even if he commits adultery and steals. I said: Even if he commits adultery and steals? He said: Even if he commits adultery and steals and drinks alcohol.” In some narrations: The one who said that was Abu Dharr to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the third time: Even if Abu Dharr’s nose is in vain. So Abu Dharr used to say after completing the hadith: Even if Abu Dharr’s nose is in vain. In some Musnads and Sunans, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: “O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and put your hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind. Even if you come to Me with sins nearly as great as the earth, I will come to you with forgiveness nearly as great as it, as long as you do not associate anything with Me, and if you make a mistake until your sins reach the clouds of the sky and then you ask My forgiveness.” I have forgiven you.” This is why there is evidence in the Qur’an, when God Almighty said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Whoever dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise. And the verses and hadiths on this are very numerous. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Ubadah and Abu al-Darda’, Do not associate anything with God, even if you cut up, crucify, or burn. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Awf Al-Himsi told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Yazid told us, Sayyar bin Abd Al-Rahman told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Qawdhar, on the authority of Salamah bin Shureih, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us with seven characteristics: Do not associate anything with God, even if you burn, cut up, or crucify. And the Almighty said: And to parents, do good meaning He commanded you and ordered you to do good to your parents, meaning that you should be good to them as the Almighty said: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, do good and some of them read: And your Lord has commanded: that you worship none but Him, and to parents, do good, meaning be good to them. And God Almighty often links between obeying Him and being good to parents as He said: “Be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do” so He commanded to be good to them even if they were polytheists according to their status. And the Almighty said: And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel, ‘Worship none but God, and to parents, do good’ and the verse, and there are many verses on this subject. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him, he said: I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Which deed is best? He said, Prayer performed on time. I said, Then what? He said, Honoring one’s parents. I said, Then what? He said, Jihad in the cause of God. Ibn Mas`ud said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) told me these things. If I had asked him for more, he would have given me more. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ and Ubadah ibn as-Samit, each of them saying, “My two friends, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) advised me, ‘Obey your parents. If they order you to leave this world for them, then do so.’” But there is a weakness in their chains of transmission, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: “And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for you and for them.” When God the Almighty recommended parents and grandparents, He followed that with treating children and grandchildren kindly, saying: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. This is because they used to kill their children as the devils suggested to them. They used to bury their daughters alive for fear of shame, and they sometimes killed some of the sons for fear of poverty. For this reason, it was reported in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which sin is the greatest? He said: To set up a rival to God when He created you. I said: Then what? He said: To kill your child for fear that he will eat with you. I said: Then what? He said: To commit adultery with your neighbor’s wife. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And the Almighty’s saying: From poverty Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said: It is poverty, meaning do not kill them because of your existing poverty. And He said in Surat al-Isra’ 17:And do not kill your children for fear of poverty meaning do not kill them for fear of poverty in the future. That is why He said there: We provide for them and for you so He began with their provision in order to care for them, meaning do not fear your poverty because of their provision, for it is from God. As for this verse, since poverty was existing, He said: We provide for you and for them because it is more important here, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed is like the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin and oppression without right, and that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about God that which you do not know’” and its interpretation has already been presented in the Almighty’s saying: And leave the outward and inward sin. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one is more jealous than God, and for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. And Abd al-Malik ibn `Umair said, on the authority of Warad, on the authority of his freedman al-Mughira, he said: Sa`d ibn `Ubadah said: If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword without hesitation. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Are you amazed at Sa`d’s jealousy? By God, I am more jealous than Sa`d, and God is more jealous than me, for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden.” They both narrated it. Kamil Abu al-`Ala’ said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, we are jealous. He said, By God, I am jealous, and God is more jealous than me, and out of His jealousy He has forbidden indecencies. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it. It meets the conditions of al-Tirmidhi, as it was narrated with this chain of transmission: The life spans of my nation will be between sixty and seventy. And the Almighty said: And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. This is something that God Almighty has explicitly prohibited, otherwise it is included in the prohibition of indecencies, both apparent and hidden. It was narrated in the two Sahihs: On the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man who bears witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God is not permissible to shed except in one of three cases: a married adulterer, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” In another version: For Muslim: And there is no god but Him, the blood of a Muslim man is not permissible, and he mentioned it. Al-A’mash said: So I told it to Ibrahim, and he told me on the authority of Al-Aswad on the authority of Aisha something similar. Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a married adulterer who is stoned to death; a man who kills intentionally who is killed; and a man who leaves Islam and wages war against God and His Messenger who is killed, crucified, or exiled from the land.” This is the wording of Al-Nasa’i. And on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he said while he was besieged: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieved after his conversion to Islam, or committed adultery after his marriage, or killed a soul without a soul.” By God, I did not commit adultery in the pre-Islamic period or in Islam. I did not wish that I had my religion in exchange for it when God guided me, nor did I kill a soul. So why do you kill me? Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith. The prohibition, warning and threat came in killing a protected person who is considered safe from the people of war. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever kills a protected person will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, although its fragrance can be detected from a distance of forty years. And on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever kills a protected person who has the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger has broken his protection of God, so he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, although its fragrance can be detected from a distance of seventy years.” Narrated by Ibn Majah and Al-Tirmidhi, who said: It is good and authentic. His statement: This is what He has enjoined upon you so that you may understand, meaning this is one of the things He has enjoined upon you so that you may understand the commands and prohibitions of God.
6:152: Ata bin Al-Sa'ib said on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said when God revealed, And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best and Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly the verse, then the one who had an orphan went and separated his food from his food and his drink from his drink, and he would keep the excess for him until he ate it and spoiled it, and that was difficult for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed, "And they ask you about orphans. Say, 'Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.'" He said: So they mixed their food with their food and their drink with their drink. Narrated by Abu Dawud. And God's statement, Until he reaches maturity, Al-Sha'bi, Malik, and more than one of the predecessors said: It means until he reaches puberty. Al-Suddi said: Until he reaches thirty years of age, and it was said forty years, and it was said sixty years. He said: All of this is far-fetched here, and God knows best. And God's statement, And give full measure and weight in justice, commands God Almighty established justice in taking and giving, as He threatened those who neglected it in His saying: “Woe to those who give less, who, when they take by measure from people, take in full, but when they give by measure or weight to them, give less. Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?” God destroyed a nation who gave less in measure and weight. In the book Al-Jami` by Abu Issa Al-Tirmidhi: From the hadith of Al-Hussein bin Qais Abu Ali Al-Rahbi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of measure and balance, You have been given charge of a matter in which the nations before you perished. Then he said: We do not know it to be traced back to the Prophet except from the hadith of Al-Hussein, and it is weak in hadith. It was narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, as a continuation of the narration. I said: Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation from the hadith of Sharik on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You, O group of Mawali, God has given you glad tidings of two characteristics by which previous generations were destroyed: the measure and the scale.” And the Almighty’s saying: We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, meaning whoever strives to perform the right and take it, if he makes a mistake after exhausting his capacity and exerting his effort, there is no blame upon him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Baqiyyah on the authority of Maysarah bin Ubaid on the authority of Amr bin Maymun bin Mihran on the authority of his father on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the verse: “And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity,” so he said: Whoever gives full measure and weight with his hand, and God knows the soundness of his intention in giving them, will not be held accountable, and that is the interpretation of its capacity. This is a strange mursal, and his saying: And when you speak, be just, even if it is a relative, is like his saying: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for God, witnesses in justice. The verse, and similar ones in Surat An-Nisa, commands justice in actions and words towards those near and far, and God commands justice for everyone at all times and in all circumstances. And His statement, And fulfill the covenant of God, Ibn Jarir said: He is saying, And fulfill the commandment of God that He has enjoined upon you. Fulfilling that means obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and acting according to His Book and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and that is fulfilling the covenant of God. This He has enjoined upon you that you may remember. God the Almighty says: This He has enjoined upon you and commanded you to do, and He has emphasized it upon you. That you may remember, meaning that you may learn a lesson and desist from what you were doing before this. Some of them read it with a shaddah on the dhal, and others with a light dhal.
6:153: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, And do not follow other paths, for they will separate you from His path, and regarding his statement, And establish the religion and do not become divided therein, and similar to this in the Qur’an, he said: God commanded the believers to be in congregation and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them that those who came before them were destroyed only by arguments and disputes in the religion of God and similar to this, as stated by Mujahid and more than one. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Al-Aswad ibn Amir Shadhan told us, Abu Bakr, he is Ibn Ayyash, told us, on the authority of Asim, he is Ibn Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, he is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line with his hand, then said, This is the straight path of God, and he drew lines to its right and left, then said, These paths, there is no path among them but that there is a devil upon it calling to it, then he recited, And this is My straight path, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path, and Al-Hakim narrated it likewise on the authority of Al-Asamm on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, and he said: It is authentic and they did not include it. And Abu Ja’far Al-Razi, Warqa’, and Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated it likewise, on the authority of Asim on the authority of Abu Wa’il, Shuqaiq Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, similarly. And Yazid ibn Harun, Musaddad, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it likewise, on the authority of Yahya ibn Habib ibn Arabi and Ibn Hibban from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, all four of them on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Asim. On the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with this chain of transmission. And Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Al-Hammani, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, with this chain of transmission. And Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi, on the authority of Sulayman bin Harb, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, with this chain of transmission likewise, and he said: It is authentic, but they did not include it. And this hadith was narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim from the hadith of Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Yunus, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it likewise from the hadith of Yahya Al-Hammani, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, with this chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Al-Hakim authenticated it as you have seen from the two chains of transmission. Perhaps this hadith is on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najud, on the authority of Zur, and on the authority of Abu Wa’il Shaqiq bin Salamah, both of them on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with this chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hakim said: The evidence for this hadith is the hadith of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, from an unreliable source, referring to the hadith that Imam Ahmad and Abd bin Hamid said, and the wording is from Ahmad: Abdullah bin Muhammad, who is Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he drew a line like this in front of him and said, This is the path of God, and two lines to his right and two lines to his left, and he said, These are the paths of Satan, then he put his hand in the middle line, then he recited this verse, “And this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. This He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous.” It was narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Majah in the Book of the Sunnah of his Sunan, and Al-Bazzar on the authority of Abu Sa’id Abdullah bin Sa’id on the authority of Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar on his authority. I said: Al-Hafiz bin Mardawayh narrated it through two chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Kindi. Abu Khalid told us on the authority of Mujalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line, and he drew a line to his right and a line to his left. He placed his hand on the middle line and recited this verse: And this is My straight path, so follow it. But the main point is on the hadith of Ibn Masoud, with what is in it of differences, if it is influential, and it was narrated as being attributed to him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Aban on the authority of Uthman, that a man said to Ibn Masoud: What is the straight path? He said: We left Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the bottom and end of Paradise, and on his right was a horse and on his left was a horse, then there were men calling whoever passed by them, and whoever took that horse, it would lead him to Hell, and whoever took the path, it would lead him to Paradise. Then Ibn Mas`ud recited: And this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path 10:13. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abu `Amr told us, Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Wahhab told us, Adam told us, Ismail ibn `Ayyash told us, Abaan ibn `Ayyash told us on the authority of Muslim ibn `Imran on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, `Abdullah asked about the straight path, and Ibn Mas`ud said: We left Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the bottom and end of Paradise, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith as mentioned above, and God knows best. It was narrated from the hadith of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an something similar to it. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Suwar Abu Al-Ala’ told me, Laith, meaning Ibn Sa’d, told us, from Mu’awiyah bin Salih, that Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair bin Nufayr told him, from his father, from Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has given an example of a straight path, and on either side of the path are two walls in which there are open doors, and over the doors are lowered curtains, and at the door of the path is a caller calling: O people, come, enter the straight path all together and do not separate. A caller calls from above the path, and if a person wants to open one of those doors, he says: Woe to you, do not open it, for if you open it you will enter it. The path is Islam, and the two walls are the limits of God and the open doors are the prohibitions of God, and that caller at the head of the path is the Book of God, and the caller from above the path is the preacher of God in the heart of every Muslim.” It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i from Ali bin Hajar. Al-Nasa’i and Amr bin Uthman both added, from Baqiyyah bin Al-Waleed from Yahya bin Sa’d. On the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nafeer, on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. God the Almighty said: So follow Him and do not follow [other] ways. He only made His way singular because the truth is one, and for this reason He gathered the ways because they are dispersed and branched, as God the Almighty said: “God is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into the light. As for those who disbelieve, their allies are false gods. They bring them out from light into darkness. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Sufyan ibn Husayn told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you will pledge allegiance to me on these three verses? Then he recited: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you,” until he finished three verses, then he said: “And whoever fulfills them, his reward is with God. And whoever omits anything from them and God overtakes him in this world, his punishment will be. And whoever delays him until the Hereafter, his affair is with God. If He wills, He will take him, and if He wills, He will pardon him.”
6:154: Ibn Jarir said: Then We gave Moses the Scripture means: Then say, O Muhammad, informing us that We gave Moses the Scripture, as indicated by His statement: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.” I said: There is a consideration in this, and then here is only for the purpose of connecting the report after the report, not for the purpose of order here, as the poet said: Tell him who became a leader, then his father became a leader, then his grandfather became a leader before that. Here, when God Almighty informed us about the Qur’an, saying, And this is My straight path, so follow it, He followed it with praise for the Torah and its Messenger, saying, Then We gave Moses the Book. God Almighty often links the mention of the Qur’an to the Torah, such as His Almighty saying, “And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in the Arabic language.” And His saying at the beginning of this surah, “Say, ‘Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance for mankind? You make it into sheets, some of which you reveal and much of which you conceal. ’” The verse, and after it, And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed. The verse. God the Almighty said, informing about the polytheists: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, ‘Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?’ God the Almighty said: Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, ‘Two magicians who backed up each other.’ And they said, ‘Indeed, we are disbelievers in both.’ God the Almighty said, informing about the jinn that they said, O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth. The verse. God the Almighty said: Completely and in detail for him who does good. That is, We gave him the Book that We revealed to him, complete and comprehensive, for what he needs in his law, as in His statement: And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things. The verse. God the Almighty said: For him who does good. That is, a reward for his good deeds and his fulfillment of Our commands and obedience, as in His statement: Is the reward for good [anything] but good? and His statement: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, He said, ‘Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.’ and His statement: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command. When they were patient and were certain of Our signs. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, Then We gave Moses the Scripture, perfecting it for him who did good. He means he did good in what God gave him. Qatada said, Whoever does good in this world, it will be completed for him in the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir chose to say, Then We gave Moses the Scripture, perfecting it for him, for his goodness, so it is as if he made which a source, as was said in the words of God Almighty, And you plunged like those who plunged, meaning like their plunge. Ibn Rawahah said: And God has confirmed what He has given you of good among the messengers and a victory like that which they have given victory. Others said: who here means those who. Ibn Jarir said: It was mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he used to recite it completely for those who did good. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: On the authority of Mujahid: completely for those who did good. He said: for the believers and the doers of good. Abu Ubaidah said the same. Al-Baghawi said: the doers of good are the prophets and the believers. He meant that we showed His favor to them. I said: Like the statement of God Almighty: He said, ‘O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and with My speech.’ It is not necessary that He chose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Seal of the Prophets and the Friend, peace be upon them, for other evidence. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Amr bin Al-Ala narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Ya`mar that he used to recite it completely on the one who is better, raising it with the interpretation of on the one who is better. Then he said: This is a reading that I do not permit reading with, even though it has a correct meaning in Arabic. It was said: Its meaning is completely on the goodness of God to him in addition to what he was good to him. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Al-Baghawi, and there is no contradiction between it and the first statement, and Ibn Jarir combined it as we explained, and praise be to God. And the Almighty’s statement: And a detailed explanation of everything and guidance and mercy contains praise for His Book that God revealed to him “Perhaps they will believe in the meeting with their Lord. And this is a blessed Book We have revealed, so follow it and fear God that you may receive mercy.” In it is the call to follow the Qur’an. God, the Almighty, encourages His servants to follow His Book and commands them to ponder it and act upon it and call to it and describe it as a blessing for those who follow it and act upon it in this world and the hereafter because it is the strong rope of God.

6:156: Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is, This is a book that We have revealed so that you will not say, ‘The Book was only revealed to two groups before us,’ meaning so that your excuse will be cut off, as God Almighty said: And had it not been that a disaster would strike them for what their hands have put forth, they would say, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs?’ 10:13. God Almighty also said, to two groups before us, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that they are the Jews and Christians, and Mujahid, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and more than one person said the same. His statement, And we were indeed unaware of their study, means that we did not understand what they were saying because they were not speaking our language, and we were unaware and busy with what they were doing. And His statement, Or you say, ‘If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they are,’ meaning, We have cut off your excuses that you should say, If only what was sent down to them had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them in what they were given, like His statement, And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the nations, the verse. And thus He said here, There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord and guidance and mercy, meaning, there has come to you from God on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Arab Prophet, a great Qur’an in which there is clarification of what is permissible and what is forbidden, guidance for what is in the hearts, and mercy from God for His servants who follow it and observe what is in it. And the Almighty said: So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away from them? That is, he did not benefit from what the Messenger brought, nor did he follow what he was sent with, nor did he abandon anything else, but turned away from following the signs of God, that is, he turned away from people and prevented them from that. This was said by al-Suddi, and from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah, And turned away from them means he turned away from them. Al-Suddi’s statement here is strong because he said: So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away from them? as mentioned earlier at the beginning of the surah, while they forbid it and keep away from it, and they do not destroy except themselves. And the Almighty said: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God - We will increase for them a punishment over the punishment. And He said in this noble verse: We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with the worst punishment for what they used to turn away. And what is meant by what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said may be: So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away from them? That is, he does not believe in them or act upon them, like the Almighty’s statement: So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. And other verses that indicate that the disbeliever includes Denying in his heart and abandoning the work with his limbs, but the words of al-Suddi are stronger and clearer, and God knows best, because God said, Who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away from them? like the Almighty’s saying, Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God - We will increase for them a punishment over the punishment because they used to cause corruption.

6:158: God Almighty says, threatening those who disbelieve in Him, oppose His messengers, deny His signs, and turn people away from His path: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come? That will happen on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Or that some of the signs of your Lord should come? That is before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before. That is before the Day of Resurrection. It is one of the signs and portents of the Hour when they see some of the portents of the Hour, as Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Musa bin Ismail told us, Abdul Wahid told us, Amara told us, Abu Zur’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When the people see it, those on it will believe.” That is when faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before. Ishaq told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. In another version: “When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe. That is when faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before.” Then he recited this verse. This hadith was narrated in this way from these two chains of transmission. From the first chain of transmission, the rest of the group included it in their books, except for al-Tirmidhi, through various chains of transmission on the authority of ‘Ammarah ibn al-Qa’qa’ ibn Shubramah, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah ibn Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on his authority. As for the second path, it was narrated by Ishaq, not attributed to him, and it was said that he is Ibn Mansur Al-Kousaj, and it was said that he is Ishaq Ibn Nasr, and God knows best. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Rafi’ Al-Jundisaburi, both of them on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, and this hadith was narrated through other paths on the authority of Abu Hurairah, just as Muslim was the only one to narrate it from the hadith of Al-Ala’ Ibn Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Ya’qub, the freed slave of Al-Harqa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that, if they appear, will not benefit a soul from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, and the beast of the earth.” Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Fadil ibn Ghazwan on the authority of Abu Hazim Salman on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and he has the same chain of transmission. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhair ibn Harb on the authority of Wakee’, and he and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from other chains of transmission on the authority of Fadil ibn Ghazwan on the authority of him. Ishaq ibn Abdullah al-Qarawi narrated it on the authority of Malik ibn Abi al-Zinad on the authority of al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurairah, but none of the authors of the books narrated it from this chain of transmission because of the weakness of al-Qarawi. And God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Shu’ayb bin Al-Layth told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Harmaz Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises, all people will believe. That is when faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before.” And Ibn Lahi’ah narrated it on the authority of Al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on his authority. And Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Fadil bin Ghazwan on the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on his authority. All of these chains of narration were included by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh in his interpretation. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever repents before the sun rises from the West, it will be accepted from him. None of the authors of the six books included it. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Dharr Al-Ghifari in the two Sahihs and others through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid bin Sharik Al-Taimi on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know where the sun goes when it sets? I said: I do not know. He said: “It stops short of the Throne, then falls down in prostration, then stands until it is told to go back. It is likely, O Abu Dharr, that it will be told to go back from whence you came. That is when ‘faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before.’” Another hadith On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid ibn Abi Sharihah al-Ghifari, may God be pleased with him, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Furat, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked out at us from a room while we were discussing the Hour. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke and the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, the emergence of the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, driving or gathering people, spending the night with them where they spent the night and resting with them where they rested.” And Muslim and the four scholars of Sunan narrated it in this way from the hadith of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl Amir ibn Wathilah, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid, on his authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, al-Thawri said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rib’i, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, what is the sign of the rising of the sun from its place of setting? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “That night will be lengthened until it is the length of two nights, then those who used to pray will wake up and do as they used to do before it, and the stars will not be seen because they have set in their place. Then they will sleep, then get up and pray, then sleep, then get up and their sides will appear to them until the night becomes long for them and the people will be frightened and they will not wake up. While they are waiting for the sun to rise from its place of rising, it will rise from its place of setting. When the people see it, they will believe, but their belief will not benefit them.” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and it is not in any of the six books from this source - and God knows best. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, whose name is Saad bin Malik bin Sinan, may God be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith, he said: The rising of the sun from its place of setting. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Wakee’, on the authority of his father, and he said: It is strange. Some of them narrated it without attributing it to the Prophet. In the hadith of Talut bin Abbad, on the authority of Fadhal bin Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Umamah Sadi bin Ajlan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first of the signs is the rising of the sun from its place of setting. In the hadith of Asim bin Abi Al-Najud, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has opened a door before sunset, seventy years wide, for repentance, and it will not be closed until the sun rises from it. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, and authenticated by Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah in a long hadith. Another hadith On the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Duhaim told us, Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Dhirar bin Sard told us, Ibn Fadil told us on the authority of Sulayman bin Yazid on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A night will come upon the people that will be equal to three of your nights. When the voluntary prayers recognize it, one of them will stand and recite his portion, then sleep. Then he will stand and recite his portion, then sleep. While they are like that, the people will shout to one another and say, ‘What is this?’ They will rush to the mosques, and they will see the sun rising, and when it is in the middle of the sky, it will return and rise from its place of rising. He said at that time: ‘Faith does not benefit a soul.’” This hadith is strange from this perspective, and it is not in any of the six books. Another hadith on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Amr bin Jarir, who said: Three men from the Muslims sat with Marwan in Medina and heard him narrating about the signs, saying that the first of them is the Antichrist. He said: So they turned to Abdullah bin Amr and told him what they had heard from Marwan about the signs, and he said: Marwan did not say anything. I memorized from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from its place of setting and the emergence of the beast at noon. Whichever of them comes before the other, the other will follow it.” Then Abdullah said: He was reading the books, and I think the first of them to appear will be the rising of the sun from its place of setting. That is because whenever it sets, it comes under the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, and He gives it permission to return. Then when it appears to God that it should rise from its place of setting, it does as it used to do, it comes under the Throne, prostrates, and asks permission to return, but nothing answers it. Then it asks permission to return, but nothing answers it. Then when the night has passed as God wills, and it knows that if it is given permission to return, it will not reach the east, it says: O Lord, how far is the east. Who will be with the people, until the horizon becomes like a necklace, then she asks permission to go back, and it is said to her: From where you are, look out, so she looks out upon the people from the west, then Abdullah recited this verse: Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before, the verse, and Muslim included it in his Sahih, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah included it in their Sunans on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, whose name is Yahya ibn Sa`id ibn Hayyan ibn Abi Zur`ah ibn `Amr ibn Jarir, on his authority. Another hadith from him Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Yahya bin Khalid bin Hayyan Al-Raqi told us: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Zuraiq Al-Himsi told us: Uthman bin Saeed bin Katheer bin Dinar told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Yahya bin Abdullah on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the sun rises from the west, Satan falls down in prostration, calling out loudly: ‘My God, command me to prostrate to whomever You wish. ’ He said: ‘Then his henchmen will gather around him and all of them will say: What is this supplication? ’ He will say: ‘I only asked my Lord to grant me respite until the appointed time, and this is the appointed time. ’ He said: ‘Then the beast of the earth will emerge from a crack in Al-Safa. ’ He said: ‘The first step it will take will be in Antioch, and it will come to Satan and slap him. ’” This is a very strange hadith and its chain of transmission is weak. Perhaps it is one of the two afflictions that Abdullah bin Amr suffered on the day of Yarmouk. As for its chain of transmission to the Prophet, it is rejected, and God knows best. Another hadith On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, Abdul Rahman bin Awf, and Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan, may God be pleased with them all. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ narrated to us, Ismail bin Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Damdam bin Shuraih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Malik bin Yakhamir, on the authority of Ibn Al-Sa’di, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Migration will not cease as long as the enemy is fighting. Muawiyah, Abdul Rahman bin Awf, and Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Migration has two characteristics, one of which is abandoning evil deeds and the other is migrating to God and His Messenger. It will not cease as long as repentance is accepted, and repentance will continue to be accepted until the sun rises from the west. When it rises, every heart will be sealed with what is in it, and people will be spared from doing good deeds.” This hadith has a good chain of transmission, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it, and God knows best. Another hadith On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him. Awf Al-A'rabi said on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, Abu Ubaidah told me on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to say that the signs mentioned have already passed except for four: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, the beast of the earth, and the emergence of Gog and Magog. He said that he used to say that the sign with which deeds are concluded is the rising of the sun from the west. Have you not seen that God says, "On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come," the entire verse means the rising of the sun from the west. The hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh in his interpretation from the hadith of Abdul-Muneem Ibn Idris, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Wahb Ibn Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. He mentioned a long, strange, and rejected hadith that he attributed to the Prophet, in which it says that the sun and the moon will rise on that day from the west, together, and when they reach the middle of the sky, they will return and then return to what they were. It is a very strange hadith, rather, it is rejected and fabricated, if it is claimed that it is traceable back to the Prophet. As for stopping it at Ibn Abbas or Wahb Ibn Munabbih, which is more likely, then it is not rejected, and God knows best. Sufyan said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Aamer on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When the first signs are revealed, the guardian angels will be thrown away and the bodies will testify to the deeds. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. So the words of God Almighty: Faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before, meaning if the disbeliever creates faith on that day, it will not be accepted from him. As for the one who was a believer before that, if he was a righteous person in his deeds, then he is doing a great good deed. But if he was not a righteous person and then repented at that time, his repentance will not be accepted from him, as indicated by the previous hadiths. This is what God Almighty’s words: or earned good through her faith, are interpreted as meaning that the earning of a righteous deed will not be accepted from her if she did not do it before that. And the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Wait, indeed, We are waiting.” This is a severe threat to the disbelievers and a definite warning to those who delay their faith and repentance until a time when it will not benefit them. Rather, this ruling was at the rising of the sun from the West due to the approach of the Hour and the appearance of its signs, as He said: “Do they then await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? But its signs have already come. So how will they be helped when their reminder has come to them?” And the Almighty’s saying: “But when they saw Our punishment, they said: We believe in God alone and we disbelieve in that with which we used to associate.” So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment.”
6:159: Mujahid, Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said that this verse was revealed about the Jews and Christians. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, that the Jews and Christians differed before the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they split up. When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, God revealed to him, Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything, the verse. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Omar Al-Sakuni told me, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibad bin Katheer wrote to me, Laith told us, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding this verse, Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - you are not of them in anything, and they are not from you. They are the people of innovations, the people of doubts and the people of misguidance from this nation. But this chain of transmission is not authentic, because Ibad bin Katheer is a rejected hadith narrator, and he did not fabricate this hadith, but he made a mistake in attributing it to the Prophet, because Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Laith, who is the son of Abi Salim, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding the verse, in which he said: It was revealed about this nation. Abu Ghalib said on the authority of Abu Umamah regarding his statement, and they were sects, he said, They are the Khawarij. It was narrated on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but it is not authentic. Shu’bah said on the authority of Mujalid on the authority of al-Sha’bi on the authority of Shuraih on the authority of ‘Umar may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to ‘Aa’ishah may God be pleased with her: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects - he said - are the people of innovations. This was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and it is also strange, and its chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is not authentic. What appears is that the verse is general in meaning and applies to everyone who has departed from the religion of God and opposed it, for God sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions, and His law is one, with no difference or division in it. So whoever differs about it and they are sects, meaning groups like the people of religions, sects, whims and misguidance, then God the Most High has disavowed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from what they are in. This verse is like His statement, He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you (al-Baqarah 2:17). And in the hadith: We, the prophets, are children of one religion. This is the straight path, which is what the messengers brought of worshipping God alone, with no partner, and adhering to the law of the later messenger. Whatever contradicts that is superstition, ignorance, opinions, and whims, and the messengers are innocent of them, as God Almighty said: You are not of them in anything. And His Almighty saying: “Their affair is only with God. Then He will inform them about what they used to do.” Like His Almighty saying: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans or Magians or polytheists - God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Then He explained His kindness, glory be to Him, in His judgment and justice on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said:
6:160: This noble verse is a detailed explanation of what is summarized in the other verse, which is His saying, Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. Hadiths have been reported that match this verse, as Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Affan told us, Ja'far bin Sulayman told us, Al-Ja'd Abu Uthman told us, on the authority of Abu Raja' Al-Attardi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, in what he narrated from his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, "Indeed, your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, is Merciful. Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed will be recorded for him. If he does it, ten to seven hundred will be recorded for him, or many times over. Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, a good deed will be recorded for him. If he does it, one good deed will be recorded for him, or God, the Almighty and Majestic, will erase it. And no one perishes on God's authority except one who perishes." Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Al-Ja'd Abu Uthman. Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: Whoever does a good deed will have ten like it and more. Whoever does a bad deed, its recompense will be the like thereof or I will forgive him. Whoever commits an earth-sized sin and then meets Me, not associating anything with Me, I will grant him forgiveness like it. Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I will draw near to him an arm’s length. Whoever draws near to Me an arm’s length, I will draw near to him an arm’s length. Whoever comes to Me walking, I will come to him running.” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on his authority, and on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Waki’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on his authority. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Muhammad Al-Tanafisi, on the authority of Waki’, on his authority. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Shaiban told us, Hammad told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, one good deed will be recorded for him. If he does it, ten good deeds will be recorded for him. Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, nothing will be recorded for him. If he does it, one bad deed will be recorded for him.” And know. The one who abandons a bad deed and does not do it is divided into three categories: Sometimes he abandons it for the sake of God, so a good deed is recorded for him for refraining from it for the sake of God the Most High, and this is an action and intention. That is why it was said that a good deed is recorded for him, as it was mentioned in some versions of the Sahih, He abandoned it because of Me, meaning for My sake. Sometimes he abandons it out of forgetfulness and heedlessness about it, so this is neither for him nor against him, because he did not intend good nor did he do evil. Sometimes he abandons it out of inability and laziness about it after striving for its causes and engaging in what brings one closer to it, so this is like the one who does it, as it was mentioned in the Sahih hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, If two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire. They said, O Messenger of God, this is the killer, so what about the killed? He said, He was eager to kill his companion. Imam Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said: Mujahid ibn Musa told us, Ali told us, and al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah and Ibn Khaithama told us, they said: Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, both of them on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ubayd God ibn Anas, on the authority of his grandfather Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever intends to do a good deed, God will write for him a good deed. If he does it, it will be written for him ten times. Whoever intends to do an evil deed, it will not be written for him until he does it. If he does it, it will be written for him a bad deed. If he abandons it, it will be written for him a good deed. God, the Most High, will say: ‘He abandoned it only out of fear of Me.’” This is the wording of the hadith of Mujahid, meaning Ibn Musa. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Shaiban ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his uncle, so-and-so ibn Umaila, on the authority of Khuraim ibn Fatik al-Asadi, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People are four in number and deeds are six. Some people are given plenty in this world and the next, some are given plenty in this world and are restricted in the next world, and some are restricted in this world and are given plenty in the next world and are miserable in this world and the next. Deeds are two types of things, and like…” “By the same, ten times, and seven hundred times. The two reasons are: whoever dies as a Muslim, believing, not associating anything with God, Paradise is obligatory for him, and whoever dies as a disbeliever, Hell is obligatory for him. Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, God knows that his heart has felt it and he is keen on it, a good deed is written for him. Whoever intends to do a bad deed, it is not written for him, and whoever does it, one is written for him and it is not multiplied for him. Whoever does a good deed, it is ten times its value. Whoever spends money in the way of God, the Almighty, it is seven hundred times.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Al-Rukayn ibn Al-Rabi’ on the authority of his father on the authority of Bashir ibn Umaila on the authority of Khuraim ibn Fatik, with some of it, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar al-Qawariri told us, Yazid ibn Zura’ told us, Habib ibn al-Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Three people attend Friday prayers: a man who attends it and prays, and he is a man who prays to God, so if He wills, He will give him, and if He wills, He will withhold from him. A man who attends it with listening and silence, and does not step over a Muslim’s neck or harm anyone, and it is an expiation for him until the following Friday, plus three days more.” This is because God Almighty says: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hisham ibn Murthad told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail told us, my father told me, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Friday is an expiation for what is between it and the following Friday, plus three days more. This is because God Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. And on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him. On his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever fasts three days of every month has fasted the entire year. Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and this is his wording, and by al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi. He added: “Then God revealed confirmation of that in His Book: ‘Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof.’ Today is ten days.” Then he said: This is a good hadith. Ibn Mas’ud said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof. Whoever brings there is no god but God, and whoever brings a bad deed says that he has polytheism. This is also narrated by a group of the Salaf, may God be pleased with them all. A hadith has been reported on this subject, and God knows best its authenticity, but I have not seen it from a source that proves it. The hadiths and reports on this are very numerous, and what has been mentioned is sufficient, God willing, and it is trustworthy.
6:161: God Almighty says, commanding His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the master of messengers, to inform of what He has bestowed upon him of guidance to His straight path, in which there is no crookedness or deviation, a straight religion, meaning one that is established and firm, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. Like His statement, And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? And His statement, “And strive in God’s cause with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty - the religion of your father Abraham.” And His statement, “Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. * Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. * And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. * Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.’” It does not follow from the fact that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded following the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, that Abraham was more perfect than him in it, because he, peace be upon him, carried it out in a great manner and it was perfected for him in a complete manner. No one preceded him in this perfection, and for this reason he was the Seal of the Prophets and the Master of the Children of Adam in general, and the possessor of the praiseworthy station that all creation desires, even Abraham, peace be upon him. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hafs told us, Ahmad ibn Issam told us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah told us, Salamah ibn Kuhail told us, I heard Dhir ibn Abdullah al-Hamadani narrating on the authority of Ibn Abza on the authority of his father, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up, he would say: “We have woken up on the religion of Islam and the word of sincerity and the religion of our Prophet Muhammad and the religion of our father Abraham, the upright one, and he was not of the polytheists.” Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: It was said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Which religion is most beloved to God Almighty? He said: The easy upright one. Ahmad also said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) placed my chin on his shoulder, so that I could look at the Abyssinian flock until I was the one who got bored and turned away from him. Abdul Rahman said on the authority of his father: Urwah told me that Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day, “So that the Jews may know that there is latitude in our religion. I have been sent with a tolerant Hanifiyah.” The original hadith is found in the two Sahihs, and the addition has supporting evidence from several chains of transmission. I have examined its chains of transmission in the explanation of Bukhari, praise and thanks be to God. God’s statement, “Say: My prayer and my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds,” commands him to inform the polytheists who worship other than God and slaughter in a name other than His, that he is opposing them in that, for his prayer and sacrifice are for God alone, with no partner. This is like God’s statement, Then pray to your Lord and sacrifice, meaning devote your prayer and sacrifice to Him, for the polytheists used to worship idols and slaughter for them. So God, the Most High, commanded him to oppose them and deviate from what they were doing and to turn with purpose, intention and resolve to be sincere to God, the Most High. Mujahid said regarding His statement, My prayer and my sacrifice, the sacrifice is slaughtering in Hajj and Umrah. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr. And my sacrifice he said, my sacrifice, and so said Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Dhahabi told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two rams on the day of Eid al-Adha and said when he slaughtered them: “I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.” And the Almighty’s statement: And I am the first of the Muslims, Qatadah said: meaning of this nation, and it is as he said, for all the prophets before him all called to Islam, and its origin is the worship of God alone, with no partner, as He said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And God Almighty informed us about Noah that he said to his al-Nas 114:“But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from God, and I have been commanded to be of the Muslims.” And God Almighty said: And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except he who makes a fool of himself? And We had chosen him in the Hereafter. And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. When his Lord said to him, Submit, he said, I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. And Abraham enjoined this upon his sons, and so did Jacob, O my sons, indeed God has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims. And Joseph, peace be upon him, said, “My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams, Creator of the heavens and the earth. You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.” And Moses said, O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims. And they said, “Upon God we have relied. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people. And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.” And God the Almighty said, “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for the Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars.” And God the Almighty said, And when I inspired to the disciples, ‘Believe in Me and in My Messenger,’ they said, ‘We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.’ So God the Almighty informed us that He sent His messengers with Islam, but they differed in it according to their own laws that Some of them abrogate others, until they were abrogated by the law of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, which will never be abrogated, and will continue to exist, victorious, and its banners will be spread until the Day of Judgment. That is why he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “We, the prophets, are the sons of the same religion. Our religion is one.” The sons of the same religion are the brothers from one father and different mothers. The religion is one, and it is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, even if the laws that are like mothers are diverse. Likewise, the brothers of the brothers are the opposite of this, the sons of one mother from different fathers, and the brothers are the full siblings from one father and one mother. And God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al Majshun told us, Abdullah bin Al Fadl Al Hashemi told us, on the authority of Al Araj, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Rafi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say the Takbir, he would begin and then say: “I have directed my face towards He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God.
