6:164: God the Almighty says, Say O Muhammad to these polytheists who associate partners with God in sincere worship of Him and trust in Him, Shall I seek a lord other than God? That is, seek a lord other than Him, while He is the Lord of all things who nurtures me, protects me, takes care of me, and manages my affairs, that is, I do not trust anyone but Him and I do not turn except to Him because He is the Lord of all things and their King, and to Him belongs creation and command. So in this verse there is the command to sincerely trust, just as the one before it included sincerely worshipping God alone, with no partner for Him. This meaning is often linked to the other in the Qur'an, such as God the Almighty's saying, guiding His servants to say to Him, You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help, and His saying, So worship Him and put your trust in Him, and His saying, Say, He is the Most Gracious, we have believed in Him, and in Him we put our trust, and His saying, Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs, and similar verses. And the Almighty’s saying: And no soul earns except against itself, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, is a report of the reality on the Day of Resurrection in the recompense of God the Almighty, His judgment and justice, that souls are only rewarded for their deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, and that no one bears the sin of another, and this is from His justice, the Almighty, as He said: And if a heavily laden one calls for its load, nothing of it will be borne by him, even if he were a relative. And the Almighty’s saying: So he will not fear injustice or deprivation, the scholars of interpretation said: meaning, he will not be wronged by having the sins of another burdened upon him, nor will he be deprived by having his good deeds diminished. And the Almighty said: Every soul is pledged for what it has earned, except the companions of the right, meaning, every soul is pledged for its bad deeds, except the companions of the right, for the blessing of their righteous deeds may return to their offspring and relatives, as He said in Surat al-Tur 52:And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds, meaning, We will join with them their offspring in the high station in Paradise. And if they did not share with them in deeds, but rather in the origin of faith, and we did not deprive them, that is, we did not diminish those noble masters from their deeds in any way until we were equal to them and those who are lower than them in status, but rather the Almighty raised them to the status of the fathers by the blessing of their deeds through His grace and favor, then He said, Every person is pledged for what he has earned, that is, from evil, and His saying, Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ, that is, work according to your status, for we are working according to what we are upon, so you will be presented and we will be presented to Him, and He will inform us and you of our deeds and your deeds and that over which we used to differ in the worldly home, like His saying, “Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.’ Say, ‘Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Opener, the Knowing.’”
6:165: God the Almighty says, And it is He who has made you successors on the earth, meaning He made you populate it generation after generation, century after century, and successor after predecessor. Ibn Zayd and others said this, like the Almighty's saying, And if We willed, We could have made you angels on the earth, succeeding one another, and His saying, And He will make you successors on the earth, and His saying, Indeed, I am placing a successor on the earth, and His saying, Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors on the earth and see how you act, and His saying, And has raised some of you above others in degrees, meaning He has differentiated between you in provisions, morals, virtues and vices, appearances, shapes and colors. And He has wisdom in that, like the Almighty's saying, We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world and have raised some of them above others in degrees that some of them may take others for service, and His saying, "See how We have preferred some of them over others. But the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference." God the Almighty says, To test you in what He has given you, meaning, to test you in what He has bestowed upon you and tried you with, to test the rich in his wealth and ask him about his gratitude, and the poor in his poverty and ask him about his patience. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “The world is sweet and green, and God has made you successors in it to see what you do, so beware of the world and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was because of women.” God the Almighty says, Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful, to warn and encourage that His reckoning and punishment is swift for those who disobey Him and oppose His messengers. And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful, to those who befriend Him and follow His messengers in what they brought of report and requests. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: To have mercy on the servants for what is in them. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God Almighty often combines these two attributes in the Qur’an, such as His saying: “And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.” And His saying: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment. And other verses that include encouragement and intimidation. Sometimes He calls His servants to Him with desire and a description of Paradise and encouragement of what He has, and sometimes He calls them to Him with fear and mention of the Fire and its punishments and torments and the Resurrection and its terrors, and sometimes with both to be effective in each according to his condition. May God make us among those who obeyed in what He commanded, and left what He forbade and warned against, and believed in what He informed. He is near, responsive, hears supplications, generous, noble, and giving. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Zuhair told us, on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the believer knew what punishment is with God, no one would hope for His Paradise. If the disbeliever knew what mercy is with God, no one would despair of Paradise. God created one hundred mercies and placed one among His creation by which they may be merciful to one another. With God are ninety-nine.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Abd al-Aziz al-Darawardi on the authority of al-Ala’, and he said: It is good. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah, and Ali ibn Hajar, all three of them on the authority of Ismail ibn Ja’far, on the authority of al-Ala’, and he also said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God created creation, He wrote in a book which is with Him above the Throne: ‘My mercy prevails over my wrath.’” And he also said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God made mercy into one hundred parts, and He kept ninety-nine parts with Him and sent down one part to the earth. From that part, the creation will be merciful to one another until the Beast is lifted up.” She kept her husband away from her child for fear that he might be afflicted with it.” Narrated by Muslim - the last interpretation of Surat Al-An’am. Praise and thanks be to God.
